title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Express emotions, give your opinion with 'I think that...', agree and disagree, and join ideas with 'and', 'but', 'because' and 'so'.
intro:
Emotions, like illnesses, *come to* or *happen to* you in Kannada: ನನಗೆ ಕೋಪ ಬಂತು 'anger came to me' = 'I got angry'; ನನಗೆ ಖುಷಿ ಆಯ್ತು 'happiness happened to me' = 'I was happy'.

To report thoughts and speech, Kannada uses the little word **ಅಂತ** *anta*, which works like quotation marks placed **after** the clause: 'he will come' ಅಂತ I think.

vocab.note: Very common: ಬೇಜಾರಾಯ್ತು 'I felt bad', ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೋಬೇಡಿ 'don't feel bad'.
Dative construction: ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು 'I know', ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'don't know', ಗೊತ್ತಾಯ್ತು 'got it'.
Formal/written; speech prefers -ಊ ... -ಊ or just listing.

phrases.en: I'm so happy / I was delighted.
What you say is true. / You're right.

grammar.title: Feelings and 'I think that...' with ಅಂತ
grammar.body:
**Feelings** use the dative experiencer with ಆಗು 'happen', ಬರು 'come' or ಇದೆ: ನನಗೆ ಖುಷಿ ಆಯ್ತು 'I was happy', ಅವಳಿಗೆ ಕೋಪ ಬಂತು 'she got angry', ನನಗೆ ಭಯ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ 'I'm scared', ನಮಗೆ ಬೇಜಾರಾಗಿದೆ 'we're sad/bored'.

**What you fear or love** is marked with **ಅಂದರೆ** (spoken ಅಂದ್ರೆ), literally 'if you say': ನನಗೆ ಹಾವು ಅಂದ್ರೆ ಭಯ 'I'm afraid of snakes', ಅವನಿಗೆ ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್ ಅಂದ್ರೆ ಪ್ರಾಣ 'he's crazy about cricket'.

**Thoughts and opinions**: put the thought as a complete sentence, then **ಅಂತ** (written ಎಂದು), then the verb of thinking/saying:
• ... ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ 'it seems that ..., I think ...' (most natural)
• ... ಅಂತ ಯೋಚಿಸ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm thinking that ...'
• ... ಅಂತ ಗೊತ್ತು 'I know that ...'
The order is often flipped in speech: ನನಗೆ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ, ಅವನು ಬರಲ್ಲ ಅಂತ.

'In my opinion' = **ನನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾರ** *nanna prakāra*.

examples.en: In my opinion, Kannada is easy.
I'm very happy to see you.

grammar.title: Joining ideas: and, or, but, because, so
grammar.body:
**And**: written ಮತ್ತು; in speech, attach **-ಊ** to each item: ನಾನೂ ಅವನೂ 'he and I', ಕಾಫಿನೂ ಟೀನೂ 'both coffee and tea'. For verbs, use the past participle **-ಇ** to chain actions: ಮನೆಗೆ ಹೋಗಿ ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದೆ 'I went home and ate'.

**Or**: ಅಥವಾ, or **-ಓ ... -ಓ**: ಇವತ್ತೋ ನಾಳೆಯೋ 'today or tomorrow'. In questions: -ಆ ... -ಆ: ಕಾಫಿನಾ ಟೀನಾ? 'coffee or tea?'.

**But**: ಆದರೆ / ಆದ್ರೆ at the start of the second clause.

**Because**: ಯಾಕೆಂದರೆ / ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ at the start of the reason, often followed by ಅದಕ್ಕೆ: ನಾನು ಬರಲ್ಲ, ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಇದೆ 'I won't come, because I have work'. More native: put the reason first and end with **-ಅದಕ್ಕೆ / -ಇದ್ದರಿಂದ**: ಕೆಲಸ ಇದೆ, ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ 'I have work, so I won't come'.

**So / therefore**: ಅದಕ್ಕೆ (spoken), ಹಾಗಾಗಿ (neutral).

examples.en: My younger sister and I will come.
The film was good, but very long.
I won't go today, because it's raining.
I was very tired, so I went to bed early.

dialogue.title: After the film
dialogue.setting: Deepa and her British friend Olivia come out of a Kannada film at a Bengaluru multiplex.

lines.speaker: Deepa
lines.en: How was the film? Did you like it?

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.native: ತುಂಬಾ ಇಷ್ಟ ಆಯ್ತು! ಆದ್ರೆ ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೇಜಾರಾಯ್ತು.
lines.roman: tumbā iṣṭa āytu! ādre koneyalli bējārāytu.
lines.en: I loved it! But the ending made me sad.

lines.speaker: Deepa
lines.native: ಯಾಕೆ? ನನಗೆ ಕೊನೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸಿತು.
lines.roman: yāke? nanage kone tumbā chennāgide anta ansitu.
lines.en: Why? I thought the ending was great.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.native: ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ ಹೀರೋ ಸತ್ತು ಹೋದ! ನನಗೆ ಅಳು ಬಂತು.
lines.roman: yākandre hīrō sattu hōda! nanage aḷu bantu.
lines.en: Because the hero died! It made me cry.

lines.speaker: Deepa
lines.native: ನಿಜ, ಪಾಪ. ಆದ್ರೆ ಅದು ನಿಜ ಜೀವನದ ಹಾಗೆ ಇತ್ತು.
lines.roman: nija, pāpa. ādre adu nija jīvanada hāge ittu.
lines.en: True, poor guy. But it was like real life.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.native: ಹೂಂ, ನೀನು ಹೇಳೋದು ಸರಿ. ಹಾಡುಗಳೂ ತುಂಬಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ವು.
lines.roman: hūṃ, nīnu hēḷōdu sari. hāḍugaḷū tumbā chennāgidvu.
lines.en: Hmm, you're right. The songs were really good too.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.native: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಅಲ್ಲ, ಆದ್ರೆ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಯ್ತು. ನನಗೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಖುಷಿ!
lines.roman: ellā alla, ādre jāsti artha āytu. nanage tumbā khuṣi!
lines.en: Not everything, but most of it. I'm so happy!

culture: ಪಾಪ *pāpa* (literally 'sin') is used constantly to express sympathy: 'poor thing!'. ಅಯ್ಯೋ ಪಾಪ is the full version. Kannada cinema (Sandalwood) has a passionate following; recent hits have reached audiences across India. Note that Kannadigas often express disagreement softly and indirectly: ನೋಡೋಣ 'let's see' or ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಷ್ಟ 'a bit difficult' can mean 'no'.

tip.title: Feelings happen "to" you
tip.body:
- The person who feels takes **-ಗೆ**: **ನನಗೆ** ಖುಷಿ ಆಯ್ತು 'I was happy', **ಅವನಿಗೆ** ಕೋಪ ಬಂತು 'he got angry'.
- The feeling **happens** (ಆಗು) or **comes** (ಬರು): ಬೇಜಾರಾಯ್ತು, ಕೋಪ ಬಂತು, or just **is**: ನನಗೆ ಖುಷಿ ಇದೆ.
- Never ನಾನು ಖುಷಿ: the feeler is always in the -ಗೆ form.

sentences.native: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮನೆಗೆ ಬಂದು ತುಂಬಾ ಸಂತೋಷ ಆಯ್ತು.
sentences.roman: nimma manege bandu tumbā santōṣa āytu.
sentences.en: It was a real pleasure coming to your home.
It's a holiday, the children are thrilled.
He has a fever? Oh, poor thing!

tip.title: What you fear or love: ಅಂದ್ರೆ
tip.body:
- Put **ಅಂದ್ರೆ** (lit. 'if you say') after the thing: ನನಗೆ ನಾಯಿ **ಅಂದ್ರೆ** ಭಯ 'I'm scared of dogs'.
- Same for love and liking: ನನಗೆ ಕಾಫಿ ಅಂದ್ರೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಇಷ್ಟ 'I love coffee'.
- The feeler still takes -ಗೆ: ಮಗು**ವಿಗೆ**, ಅಮ್ಮ**ನಿಗೆ**.

sentences.en: The baby is scared of thunder.
The child is shy and won't talk.

tip.title: "I think that…" with ಅಂತ
tip.body:
- Say the thought as a full sentence, then **ಅಂತ**, then the thinking verb: ಅವನು ಬರ್ತಾನೆ **ಅಂತ** ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ 'I think he'll come'.
- … ಅಂತ ಗೊತ್ತು 'I know that …', … ಅಂತ ಯೋಚಿಸ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm thinking of …', … ಅಂತ ಹೇಳ್ತಾರೆ 'they say that …'.
- 'I know' is **ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು**, 'I don't know' ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ.

sentences.native: ಇದು ಸರಿ ಅಲ್ಲ ಅಂತ ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು.
sentences.roman: idu sari alla anta nanage gottu.

sentences.en: Do you know where they are?
I'm thinking of going to Mysuru.

sentences.native: ಈ ಹೋಟೆಲ್ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ ಅಂತ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಹೇಳ್ತಾರೆ.
sentences.roman: ī hōṭel chennāgide anta ellā hēḷtāre.
sentences.en: Everyone says this restaurant is good.

sentences.native: ಈ ಬಸ್ಸು ಜಯನಗರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಲ್ಲ ಅಂತ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ.
sentences.roman: ī bassu jayanagarakke hōgalla anta ansutte.
sentences.en: I don't think this bus goes to Jayanagar.
Think it over and tell me.
What he's saying is a lie.
Tell me the truth, what happened?

tip.title: Joining words
tip.body:
- **And**: ಮತ್ತು in writing; in speech add **-ಊ** to each: ಅಮ್ಮ**ನೂ** ಅಪ್ಪ**ನೂ** 'Mum and Dad'.
- **Or**: ಅಥವಾ, or **-ಓ … -ಓ**: ಬಸ್ಸ**ಲ್ಲೋ** ಆಟೋದ**ಲ್ಲೋ**; in questions **-ಆ … -ಆ**: ಇಡ್ಲಿ**ನಾ** ದೋಸೆ**ನಾ**?
- **But**: **ಆದರೆ** (spoken ಆದ್ರೆ) starts the second part.

sentences.en: Mum and Dad are both at home.

sentences.native: ನಾನು ಬರ್ತೀನಿ, ಆದ್ರೆ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ತಡ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ.
sentences.roman: nānu bartīni, ādre svalpa taḍa āgutte.
sentences.en: I'll come, but I'll be a bit late.
Let's go by bus or by auto.
I don't agree, but never mind.
Go home and get some rest.

tip.title: Because and so
tip.body:
- **Why?** = **ಯಾಕೆ**: ನೀವು ಯಾಕೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ?
- **Because** = **ಯಾಕೆಂದರೆ** (spoken ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ) before the reason: ಬರಲ್ಲ, ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ.
- More Kannada-like: reason first, then **ಅದಕ್ಕೆ** 'so, that's why': ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ, ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ.

sentences.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಬರಲ್ಲ, ಯಾಕಂದ್ರೆ ನನಗೆ ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ.
sentences.roman: ivattu baralla, yākandre nanage jvara ide.
sentences.en: I won't come today, because I have a fever.
It's raining, so I'm taking an auto.
Because there are so many cars on the road.

sentences.native: ನಾನು ಕನ್ನಡ ಕಲೀತಿದ್ದೀನಿ, ಯಾಕೆಂದರೆ ನನ್ನ ಹೆಂಡತಿ ಮೈಸೂರಿನವರು.
sentences.roman: nānu kannaḍa kalītiddīni, yākendare nanna heṇḍati maisūrinavaru.
sentences.en: I'm learning Kannada because my wife is from Mysuru.

sentences.native: ಅವಳಿಗೆ ಖಾರ ಇಷ್ಟ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಇಡ್ಲಿ ತಿಂತಾಳೆ.
sentences.roman: avaḷige khāra iṣṭa illa, adakke iḍli tintāḷe.
sentences.en: She doesn't like spicy food, so she eats idli.
